I scanned the passage for padded negation and restatement, where deleting the negative half or the restated half loses nothing.

1. "Access checks default to fail-closed, rather than open. Fail-closed is the only acceptable default for those checks, end of story." The "rather than open" contrast is implied by fail-closed, and the next sentence restates the same claim. I'll collapse them into one sentence.

2. "Mean time to contain fell from 18 hours to 3 hours after the playbook change, which streamlines containment. The playbook change significantly reduces mean time to contain." The second sentence restates the first with no new fact, so I'll delete it.

3. "Those privilege limits are imposed on purpose, rather than by accident." The negative half adds nothing checkable, so I'll reduce it to "Those privilege limits are imposed on purpose."

4. "Cybersecurity today is not merely an IT concern; it is a multidimensional discipline..." The positive half carries the claim on its own, so the negative windup can go.

5. "Positive reinforcement for reporters is now a standing practice, full stop." This is emphasis rather than negation or restatement, so it stays.

6. "Cyber threats have multiplied both in number and sophistication" is not padded negation, so it stays.
